title: Refactor multistep processor into a Processor class
description: Brownfield Python refactor: extract the process/batch_process logic from module-level functions into a Processor class with a configurable max_retries attribute.

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor src/processor.py. All existing tests must still pass.

1. Define a Processor class:
   class Processor:
       def __init__(self, max_retries: int) -> None
       def process(self, items: list[str]) -> list[str]
         — same retry logic as the current module-level process()
       def batch_process(self, groups: dict[str, list[str]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]
         — delegates to self.process()

2. Keep the module-level functions as thin wrappers:
   _default_processor = Processor(MAX_RETRIES)
   def process(items): return _default_processor.process(items)
   def batch_process(groups): return _default_processor.batch_process(groups)

3. Keep the module-level _transform(s) helper (unchanged).

All existing tests must still pass — callers importing process/batch_process from src.processor must work identically.
Run: pytest
required_artifacts: Module-level process() and batch_process() delegate to _default_processor
Processor(1).process(['']) raises ValueError on invalid items
followup_prompts: Run `pytest` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `pytest` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
